endpoint.text: Sensitivity and specificity vs OctreoScan (In 111 pentetreotide) with a non-inferiority endpoint (primary); change in patient management (secondary).

citations.quote: The sponsor chose the currently FDA approved test, OctreoScan, as the comparator assessing its performance in terms of sensitivity and specificity as the primary endpoint as compared to a standard of truth (conventional imaging). The division agreed to the use of OctreoScan as the comparator and a non-inferiority endpoint. Change in patient management was chosen as a secondary endpoint.

result.text: Among 78 patients with available CT/MR and In 111 pentetreotide images, Ga 68 dotatate PET agreed with CT/MR in 74 patients. Of 50 patients with NETs localized by CT/MR, Ga 68 dotatate was positive in 48 (including 13 in whom In 111 pentetreotide was negative) and was negative in 26 of 28 patients in whom CT/MR was negative.

indication.text: NETSPOT, after radiolabeling with Ga 68, is a radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for use with positron emission tomography (PET) for localization of somatostatin receptor positive neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) in adult and pediatric patients.

target_moa.text: Ga 68 dotatate binds to somatostatin receptors, with highest affinity for subtype 2 receptors (sstr2), which are overexpressed by many neuroendocrine tumor cells; PET images reflect the presence and density of somatostatin receptors, and Gallium 68 is a positron-emitting radionuclide enabling PET imaging.

citations.quote: Ga 68 dotatate binds to somatostatin receptors, with highest affinity for subtype 2 receptors (sstr2). It binds to cells that express somatostatin receptors including malignant cells, which overexpress sstr2 receptors. Gallium 68 (68Ga) is a \beta^+ emitting radionuclide with an emission yield that allows positron emission tomography (PET) imaging.

Ga 68 dotatate binds to somatostatin receptors. Based upon the intensity of the signals, PET images obtained using Ga 68 dotatate indicate the presence and density of somatostatin receptors in tissues.

summary.text: NETSPOT was submitted as a 505(b)(2) NDA supported by published literature and the retrospective adaptation of the Vanderbilt (VUMC) expanded access clinical experience. The application received priority review and orphan drug designation for use as a diagnostic for the clinical management of NETs; because of the orphan designation the pediatric assessment requirement was exempt. It was approved first cycle effective June 1, 2016.
